newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks close down on FOMC, scandal worries.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks close down on FOMC, scandal worries.

text.p: Tokyo stocks closed with hefty losses on Tuesday as a mixture of trepidation ahead of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting and anxiety over the Nomura Securities Co Ltd scandal, which media reports say is widening, weighed on the market, brokers said.
The 225-share Nikkei average sagged 2.08 percent or 429.44 percent to finish the day at 20,175.52. Its September futures tumbled 470 points to end at 20,100.

"Nikkei 225 futures in Singapore and Osaka were battered a bit by scandal worries which in turn, brought down cash stocks. There really weren't any sectors which were being traded actively and the thin trade ahead of the FOMC meeting magnified losses," a broker at a "Big Four" brokerage said. "It's hard to pin down the weakness today on just one factor."
Turnover was a 341 million shares, a shade larger than the thin 317 million shares traded on Monday.
